answerToSection18: Yes, on the state side; no on the identity side. In every order and timing probed (216 cells at four time zones, three-break short-return grids, duplicates, named, by-report-id, unknown and reused names) two different interruptions never shared an identity and a correction of the same interruption (named, by report id, or a duplicate) was never recorded as a new episode. But on a normal V1 path a separate later interruption starts from the week start the earlier interruption's return stored (its conditional projection, including return steps never executed) instead of what the athlete executed: after a return whose re-entry week was neither finished nor reviewed, any unrelated decision dated between the end of that week and the second break (an equipment statement, even a no-op one, or a systemic-fatigue report) makes stateAtBreak treat that planned start as earned (QE-R7AF-01). Founder 0.5 excludes exactly 'stateAtStartOfWeek' and 'stateStoredByPreviousReturn'.

findings.what: stateAtBreak's earned-week predicate (src/r6-adaptation.mjs:674) counts ANY decision with fromWeek <= k dated on/after the last day of week k-1 as earning week k's planned start, including an EQUIPMENT_CHANGE (fromWeek=w, strength-only, keeps the start; also a recorded KEEP) and a SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE REDUCE (fromWeek=w), none of which recomputes the start from evidence. After A's return (re-entry week unreviewed and unfinished), one such decision before a separate break B makes B's state point WEEK_START of the next week, equal field-for-field (lastPerformed and bookkeeping aside) to the start A's return stored: run and every strength exercise at return step 1, never executed. Control (no decision): RETURN/A + executed facts, step 0. Rows after B: week 6 EASY 30/LONG 45 vs 15/20; week 7 back-squat 2x5@3 KNOWN 82.5 (return complete) and LONG 60 vs back-squat 1x5@4 RETURN_ENTRY and LONG 45. P30b: 13 of 15 cells change B's start, 7 advance the run return step; a Monday fatigue report raises the post-B dose. On the byte-exact FREEZE-1 copy every cell (control included) gives step 1, so the sporting output equals R7-A.2's (SSCTR-accepted) on this path; the R7AF rule (F-B, P5) holds only 'when nothing else was decided'. Violates Founder 0.5 ('NÃO stateAtStartOfWeek nem stateStoredByPreviousReturn'), §10 (planned-not-executed progress), I5, P5 and §13 'Distinct episode — cross week … semanticamente equivalente'. Identity is correct (B NEW, own episode) in every cell.

findings.whyIdentityDidNotResolveIt: Identity decides which interruption a report is about and which report of the earlier one was in force at the break; it is right in every probe. Whether a week start between that report and the break was earned is a separate predicate that reads decision dates, not what the decision did to the start.
findings.smallestArchitecturalDecision: Decide what makes a planned week start an executed state point after a return: (a) only a decision that set that start from the executed evidence of the week before (the weekly review's rule) — record who set each week's start (RETURN | EVIDENCE | PLAN) and accept only RETURN or EVIDENCE (the contract's own wording; smallest); (b) never a planned week start after a return, always read facts forward from the return's entry; or (c) accept the plan's start after a return as before any return (C3/B3) and withdraw F-B/P5 there — contrary to 0.5's text, a Founder call.

findings.class: same class (QE-R7A1-09 outcome) through explicit identity
findings.what: A named correction (A's episodeId, or A's report event id) can move an interruption past its own executed re-entry: after A (16 days) and Tue/Wed re-entry sessions executed, a Thu-Fri trip reported with A's name is SAME_BREAK EXPLICIT of A; A becomes a 2-day SHORT break with point WEEK_START/w5 (start before A) and the next day plans back-squat 3x5@3 KNOWN 82.5 and LONG 70 — the executed re-entry erased. The contract guards crossing the previous interruption's re-entry (B4) but not the interruption's own; the author's test of this move has no executed re-entry. Not material: Founder 0.4 puts explicit update first and 0.2 lets a correction change start/end/duration; a Founder decision is needed on whether such a correction should be asked (I9).

findings.class: pre-existing (identical on FREEZE-1); accepted rule C5/QE-R7A1-03
findings.what: A same-record duplicate under a new event id is a SAME_BREAK DUPLICATE revision (one episode, correct) that re-derives the return; sent in week 7 after the re-entry weeks were executed and reviewed, it restarts a completed return (week 7 QUALITY 34 / back-squat 2x5@3 KNOWN -> RETURN_ENTRY 1x5@4, runs 15/15/20). Founder 0.4 says 'DEDUPE'; only the same event id dedupes. Conservative; product decision whether unchanged facts (equal inputHash and re-derived start) should KEEP.

staleReturn asks for confirmation (blocking every non-return review) when a late fact changes only last-performed dates (5 exercises), which contract §4 treats as immaterial for the same day. Conservative over-ask; may be noisy for athletes who sync late.
